title: The First Book of Samuel Timeline
sub: Hannah's Prayer · Saul Rejected, David Anointed
desc: Israel's transition from judges to monarchy runs through a barren woman's prayer, a boy who hears his name in the night, a rejected first king, and a shepherd who kills a giant on his way to becoming Israel's most celebrated ruler.

eras.label: Era One · 1 Samuel 1
eras.name: Hannah's Prayer for a Son
eras.dates: A barren, tormented woman pours out her soul before the LORD and vows to dedicate the son she's asking for entirely to his service

events.title: I Asked the LORD for Him: Samuel Dedicated Before Birth
events.detail: Tormented by her rival wife's taunts over her childlessness, Hannah prays so fervently at Shiloh that the priest Eli mistakes her for drunk; her vow to dedicate any son to the LORD's service is answered with Samuel's birth, and she keeps her word, bringing him to Shiloh once weaned.

verses.text: “For this boy I prayed, and the LORD [Yahweh] has given me the request that I asked of him.”

eras.label: Era Two · 1 Samuel 2
eras.name: Hannah's Song — Eli's Wicked Sons
eras.dates: A mother's prayer of praise, later echoed in Mary's Magnificat, is set against a scathing account of corrupt priestly greed

events.title: The LORD Kills and Gives Life: Hannah's Song of Praise
events.detail: Hannah's prayer of praise celebrates a God who reverses fortunes (humbling the proud, lifting the poor from the dust) in poetry that anticipates Mary's Magnificat centuries later.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] both kills and gives life; he brings down to the grave and raises up.”

events.title: Eli's Sons Treated the LORD's Offering With Contempt
events.detail: Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas abuse their priestly office, seizing meat by force and sleeping with women at the tabernacle entrance; a prophet warns Eli that his family's priestly line will be judged, with both sons destined to die on the same day.

verses.text: “The sin of these young men was very great in the LORD's sight, for they treated the LORD's offering with contempt.”

eras.label: Era Three · 1 Samuel 3
eras.name: The LORD Calls Samuel
eras.dates: A boy sleeping near the ark hears his name called in the night, not recognizing the voice until an old priest helps him understand

events.title: Speak, LORD, for Your Servant Is Listening
events.detail: The LORD calls young Samuel three times in the night before Eli realizes what's happening and instructs him how to respond, and Samuel receives his first prophetic message: a hard word of judgment against Eli's own household.

verses.text: “Eli said to Samuel, ‘Go lie down, and if he calls you, say, “Speak, LORD [Yahweh], for your servant is listening.”’”

eras.label: Era Four · 1 Samuel 4
eras.name: The Ark Captured — Ichabod
eras.dates: Treating the ark as a magic talisman rather than the presence of the LORD himself, Israel loses both the battle and the ark, and Eli's household is wiped out in a single day

events.title: The Glory Has Departed From Israel
events.detail: Israel brings the ark into battle hoping it will guarantee victory, but the Philistines capture it and kill Hophni and Phinehas; the news kills Eli instantly, and his dying daughter-in-law names her newborn son Ichabod, meaning the glory has departed.

verses.text: “The glory has departed from Israel, because the ark of God [Elohim] has been captured.”

eras.label: Era Five · 1 Samuel 5-6
eras.name: The Ark Among the Philistines — Dagon Falls
eras.dates: Far from being a Philistine trophy, the captured ark topples their god and afflicts every city that houses it, until they beg to send it home

events.title: Dagon Falls Before the Ark: the Philistine Cities Struck With Sores
events.detail: Wherever the Philistines take the captured ark, their god Dagon topples and shatters before it, and the local population is struck with plague, forcing the Philistines to pass the ark from city to city in growing panic.

verses.text: “The ark of the God of Israel should not remain with us, for he has attacked both us and our god Dagon!”

events.title: The Ark Sent Home on a New Cart
events.detail: After seven months of plague, the Philistines send the ark back to Israel with a guilt offering, testing whether their affliction was truly from the God of Israel; the ark's return is marred when curious men of Beth Shemesh look inside it and are struck down.

verses.text: “Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? To whom will the ark go up from here?”

eras.label: Era Six · 1 Samuel 7
eras.name: Ebenezer — Up to Here the LORD Has Helped Us
eras.dates: Twenty years after the ark's return, genuine national repentance under Samuel's leadership produces a decisive victory over the Philistines

events.title: Up to Here the LORD Has Helped Us
events.detail: Samuel calls Israel to put away foreign gods and genuinely return to the LORD; when the Philistines attack during a gathering at Mizpah, the LORD thunders against them and Israel wins decisively, memorialized by a stone Samuel names Ebenezer.

verses.text: “Samuel took a stone… and named it Ebenezer, saying, ‘Up to here the LORD [Yahweh] has helped us.’”

eras.label: Era Seven · 1 Samuel 8
eras.name: Israel Demands a King
eras.dates: Aging and with corrupt sons of his own, Samuel faces a request that the LORD identifies as a rejection of his own kingship over Israel

events.title: It Is Not You They Have Rejected, But Me
events.detail: Israel's elders demand a king like the other nations, and the LORD tells Samuel this is really a rejection of his own kingship; Samuel warns in detail what a human king will cost them, but the people insist anyway.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Samuel, ‘Listen to the voice of the people… it is not you that they have rejected, but it is me.’”

eras.label: Era Eight · 1 Samuel 9-10
eras.name: Saul Anointed King
eras.dates: A search for lost donkeys leads an unassuming Benjaminite directly to the prophet who secretly anoints him Israel's first king

events.title: Saul's Search for Donkeys Leads to Samuel
events.detail: Saul, a tall and handsome Benjaminite, goes looking for his father's lost donkeys and ends up at Samuel's town, where the LORD had already told the prophet a man from Benjamin would arrive that very day: the man he would anoint as Israel's king.

verses.text: “I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin. You must consecrate him as a leader over my people Israel.”

events.title: Is Even Saul Among the Prophets?: Chosen by Lot
events.detail: Samuel privately anoints Saul with oil, and a series of confirming signs culminates in the Spirit of the LORD rushing on him so he prophesies unexpectedly; publicly, Saul is chosen by lot before all Israel, though he's found hiding among the baggage.

verses.text: “Do you see the one whom the LORD has chosen? Indeed, there is no one like him among all the people.”

eras.label: Era Nine · 1 Samuel 11-12
eras.name: Saul's First Victory — Samuel's Farewell
eras.dates: A decisive rescue of a besieged city confirms Saul's kingship, followed by Samuel's own farewell address defending his integrity as leader

events.title: Saul Delivers Jabesh Gilead: the Kingship Renewed at Gilgal
events.detail: When the Ammonites threaten to gouge out the eyes of every man in Jabesh Gilead, Saul musters Israel and delivers a decisive victory, after which the kingship is formally renewed with celebration at Gilgal.

verses.text: “No one will be killed on this day. For today the LORD has given Israel a victory!”

events.title: Samuel's Farewell: Far Be It From Me to Stop Praying for You
events.detail: Samuel defends his own integrity as leader before transitioning power, then warns Israel that both king and people must still fear and obey the LORD, calling down thunder in the middle of harvest as a sign of how seriously they should take the warning.

verses.text: “Far be it from me to sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you! I will instruct you in the way that is good and upright.”

eras.label: Era Ten · 1 Samuel 13-14
eras.name: Saul's Unlawful Sacrifice — Jonathan's Daring Raid
eras.dates: An impatient king oversteps his authority just as his son proves that the LORD's deliverance needs no numerical advantage at all

events.title: Saul's Kingdom Will Not Continue: an Unlawful Sacrifice
events.detail: Facing a terrified, dwindling army and Samuel's delay, Saul offers a sacrifice himself rather than wait for the priest: a boundary violation that costs him the dynasty the LORD would otherwise have established through his line.

verses.text: “Your kingdom will not continue. The LORD has sought out for himself a man who is loyal to him.”

events.title: Nothing Can Prevent the LORD From Delivering, by Many or by a Few
events.detail: Jonathan and his armor-bearer alone attack a Philistine garrison, trusting the LORD to deliver regardless of numbers, triggering a rout that Saul nearly ruins with a rash battlefield oath that almost costs Jonathan his life.

verses.text: “Perhaps the LORD will intervene for us. Nothing can prevent the LORD from delivering, whether by many or by a few.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · 1 Samuel 15
eras.name: Saul Rejected Over Amalek
eras.dates: A commanded total destruction is only partially carried out, and Samuel delivers one of the Bible's most quoted statements on obedience over ritual

events.title: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice
events.detail: Commanded to completely destroy the Amalekites, Saul instead spares their king and the best livestock, rationalizing it as sacrifice material; Samuel rebukes him with one of Scripture's clearest statements that obedience matters more than ritual, and formally announces the LORD's rejection of Saul as king.

verses.text: “Does the LORD [Yahweh] take pleasure in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as he does in obedience? Certainly, obedience is better than sacrifice.”

eras.label: Era Twelve · 1 Samuel 16
eras.name: David Anointed — the LORD Looks at the Heart
eras.dates: Passing over seven older, more impressive brothers, Samuel anoints the overlooked youngest son of Jesse as Israel's next king

events.title: People Look at the Outward Appearance, But the LORD Looks at the Heart
events.detail: Samuel is sent to Jesse's house in Bethlehem, where seven impressive sons are rejected before the youngest, David, still tending sheep, is anointed, and immediately afterward begins serving in Saul's court playing the lyre to soothe the king's torment.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Samuel, ‘Don't be impressed by his appearance… people look on the outward appearance, but the LORD [Yahweh] looks at the heart.’”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · 1 Samuel 17
eras.name: David and Goliath
eras.dates: A shepherd boy armed with nothing but a sling faces down a nine-foot champion who has terrified Israel's entire army for forty days

events.title: The Battle Is the LORD's: Goliath Falls
events.detail: While Saul's army cowers before Goliath's daily taunts, David arrives to bring supplies to his brothers and volunteers to fight, refusing Saul's armor for his sling and five stones, declaring the battle belongs to the LORD before felling the giant with a single throw.

verses.text: “I am coming against you in the name of the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies, the God [Elohim] of Israel's armies, whom you have defied!”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · 1 Samuel 18-19
eras.name: David and Jonathan — Saul's Jealous Rage
eras.dates: A deep friendship forms between the prince and the shepherd-turned-warrior even as the king's jealousy curdles into repeated attempts on David's life

events.title: Saul Has Struck Down His Thousands, But David His Ten Thousands
events.detail: Jonathan's soul becomes bound to David's in friendship, but a victory song comparing David favorably to Saul plants a seed of murderous jealousy in the king, who begins scheming to have David killed by Philistine hands through a dangerous bride price.

verses.text: “The women who were playing the music sang, ‘Saul has struck down his thousands, but David his tens of thousands!’”

events.title: Michal Lowers David Through a Window
events.detail: Saul's jealousy escalates into direct attempts to kill David, first with a thrown spear and then with assassins sent to his house; David's wife Michal helps him escape through a window, and even Saul himself is overcome by the Spirit and prophesies when he pursues David to Samuel.

verses.text: “If you do not save yourself tonight, tomorrow you will be dead!”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · 1 Samuel 20-21
eras.name: Jonathan's Covenant — David Flees to Nob
eras.dates: A secret arrow-signal confirms Saul's murderous intent, and David's flight begins with holy bread and a captured enemy's sword

events.title: The LORD Be Between Me and You Forever: the Arrow Signal
events.detail: Jonathan tests his father's intentions and confirms through a prearranged arrow signal that Saul means to kill David, renewing his covenant of loyalty with David's family before the two part in tears.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] will be between me and you and between my descendants and your descendants forever.”

events.title: David Flees to Nob: Pretends Insanity Before Achish
events.detail: David receives holy bread and Goliath's own sword from the priest Ahimelech at Nob, then flees to Philistine territory where he narrowly escapes danger by feigning madness before King Achish of Gath.

verses.text: “He altered his behavior in their presence. Since he was in their power, he pretended to be insane.”

eras.label: Era Sixteen · 1 Samuel 22-23
eras.name: Doeg's Massacre — David Delivers Keilah
eras.dates: An informant's report triggers the slaughter of an entire priestly town, even as David continues risking his life to protect Israelite cities from the Philistines

events.title: Doeg Massacres the Priests of Nob
events.detail: Doeg the Edomite reports that the priest Ahimelech helped David, and Saul orders the entire priestly town of Nob massacred when his own guards refuse; only one priest, Abiathar, escapes to join David.

verses.text: “So Doeg the Edomite turned and struck down the priests. He killed on that day 85 men who wore the linen ephod.”

events.title: David Delivers Keilah: Saul's Pursuit Interrupted
events.detail: Even as a fugitive, David rescues the town of Keilah from Philistine raiders, consulting the LORD through the ephod at every step; Saul's relentless pursuit through the wilderness is interrupted only by a sudden Philistine raid elsewhere.

verses.text: “Saul looked for him all the time, but God did not deliver David into his hands.”

eras.label: Era Seventeen · 1 Samuel 24
eras.name: Saul's Robe Cut in the Cave
eras.dates: David gets the perfect opportunity to kill his pursuer in a cave and refuses to touch the LORD's anointed, cutting only a corner of his robe

events.title: I Will Not Extend My Hand Against My Lord
events.detail: Saul unknowingly enters the very cave where David and his men are hiding; David's men urge him to kill his pursuer, but he only cuts a corner off Saul's robe, and his conscience troubles him even for that small act against the LORD's anointed.

verses.text: “Afterward David's conscience bothered him because he had cut off an edge of Saul's robe.”

eras.label: Era Eighteen · 1 Samuel 25
eras.name: Nabal and Abigail
eras.dates: A foolish rich man's insult nearly triggers a massacre, until his wise wife intervenes and later becomes David's own wife

events.title: Abigail Prevents David From Shedding Innocent Blood
events.detail: The wealthy but foolish Nabal insults David's men after they had protected his flocks for free, provoking David to march for revenge; Nabal's wise wife Abigail intercepts him with gifts and wisdom, and after Nabal dies of shock, David marries her.

verses.text: “David said to Abigail, ‘Praised be the LORD [Yahweh], the God [Elohim] of Israel, who has sent you this day to meet me!’”

eras.label: Era Nineteen · 1 Samuel 26
eras.name: Saul's Spear and Water Jug
eras.dates: A second chance to kill Saul is again refused, this time by sneaking into his camp and taking only the spear and water jug by his head

events.title: Who Can Extend His Hand Against the LORD's Chosen One?
events.detail: David sneaks into Saul's sleeping camp with Abishai and again refuses to kill him, taking only his spear and water jug as proof of the missed opportunity, prompting Saul's temporary, tearful acknowledgment of his own wrongdoing.

verses.text: “Don't kill him! Who can extend his hand against the LORD's chosen one and remain guiltless?”

eras.label: Era Twenty · 1 Samuel 27-29
eras.name: David Among the Philistines
eras.dates: Exhausted by the chase, David takes refuge among Israel's enemies, raiding hostile tribes while deceiving his Philistine host, until other Philistine commanders refuse to trust him in battle

events.title: David Settles in Philistine Territory
events.detail: Weary of Saul's endless pursuit, David defects to King Achish of Gath, settling in Ziklag and conducting raids against Israel's other enemies while deceiving Achish into thinking he's attacking his own people.

verses.text: “One of these days I'm going to be swept away by the hand of Saul! There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines.”

events.title: The Witch of Endor: Saul Consults the Dead Samuel
events.detail: Desperate and unable to get any answer from the LORD, Saul disguises himself and consults a medium at Endor, who conjures up Samuel's spirit to deliver a final, devastating prophecy: Saul and his sons will die the next day.

verses.text: “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” Saul replied, “God has turned away from me. He does not answer me anymore.”

events.title: The Philistine Commanders Refuse to Trust David
events.detail: As the Philistines prepare for battle against Israel, their commanders refuse to let David and his men march with them, fearing he might turn on them mid-battle, sparing David from the impossible position of fighting against his own people.

verses.text: “Send the man back! Let him return to the place that you assigned him! Don't let him go down with us into the battle.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-One · 1 Samuel 30
eras.name: Ziklag Raided — David Strengthens Himself in the LORD
eras.dates: Returning home to find their city burned and families taken captive, David's men consider stoning him, until he finds strength in the LORD and pursues total recovery

events.title: David Strengthened Himself in the LORD: Everything Recovered
events.detail: David returns to find Ziklag burned and everyone's families taken by Amalekite raiders; with his own men threatening to stone him, David finds strength in the LORD, pursues the raiders, and recovers absolutely everything that was taken, establishing a lasting rule about sharing plunder equally.

verses.text: “David was very upset, for the men were thinking of stoning him… but David drew strength from the LORD [Yahweh] his God [Elohim].”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Two · 1 Samuel 31
eras.name: The Death of Saul
eras.dates: The book closes on Mount Gilboa, where Israel's first king falls on his own sword rather than face capture, ending his reign in complete defeat

events.title: Saul Falls on His Own Sword
events.detail: Defeated and wounded on Mount Gilboa, with his sons already dead, Saul takes his own life rather than be captured and tortured by the Philistines; the grateful men of Jabesh Gilead, whom Saul had once rescued, recover his body and give him an honorable burial.

verses.text: “Saul said to his armor-bearer, ‘Draw your sword and stab me with it! Otherwise these uncircumcised people will come, stab me, and torture me.’”
